target.title: fix: keep channel auto-restart after abort race during backoff
target.body:
Closes #109659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators would lose a channel permanently after a normal provider close when auto-restart backoff raced the dying run's abort signal. Gateway and container health checks stayed green while the channel never came back until a manual process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auto-restart now owns its own backoff abort lifecycle instead of sharing the dying run's `AbortSignal`. Intentional stops cancel that restart-owned supervisor, and abnormal exits clear `restartPending` with a diagnostic instead of an empty catch. No config, protocol, or public API changes.

## User Impact

When a channel connection drops, automatic restart remains reliable even if the previous run abort fires during backoff. Operators no longer need a manual gateway/container restart solely because the restart chain was swallowed silently. Intentional stops still cancel pending restarts.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox not used). Head after merge with current main: `1fae8667e`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 51 passed (exact post-merge head)

# Live gateway proof (PR head build, isolated state dir, real Telegram bot token from local config)
# Gateway: node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 19711 --bind loopback
# Provider close simulated via temporary unauthorized bot token (Telegram getMe 401),
# then manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff continued the chain.
```

New/updated regression coverage:
- restart backoff sleep signal is not the dying run abort
- manual stop during backoff clears `restartPending`
- startAccount failure does not permanently kill the restart chain
- stop during restart-owned backoff clears pending without a second start

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: channel auto-restart no longer dies silently when abort races the restart backoff sleep; `restartPending` is reconciled and failures are logged; restart-owned backoff continues after a real provider close
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw PR head `1fae8667e` (merged onto current main), isolated gateway on loopback port 19711 with real Telegram channel (`@openclawwuqxuanbot`), token auth, no secrets in logs
- Current-main contrast: on main, `restart.next(abort.signal)` binds backoff to the dying run abort and `catch {}` swallows rejections, so a stop/abort during backoff can leave `restartPending: true` with no further `startChannelInternal` and no log. After this patch, backoff uses `restart.next()` (restart-owned signal only), `stopChannel` calls `restarts.get(rKey)?.cancel()`, and the catch path clears pending / logs failures
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `git merge origin/main` onto the PR branch; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` → **51 passed**
  2. Build+start gateway from this head with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / config enabling Telegram only
  3. Observe Telegram provider start (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`, polling ingress started)
  4. Apply a temporary unauthorized bot token via `config.apply` to force a real Telegram provider close (`getMe` 401 / `channel exited`)
  5. Observe manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt N/10 in Xs`) continuing across attempts instead of a silent permanent stop
  6. `channels.stop` during healthy run returns `stopped: true` with `restartPending: false` (intentional stop)
  7. Restore valid bot token; Telegram starts again (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`)
- Evidence after fix (redacted gateway stdout excerpt):

```text
[gateway] http server listening (... telegram; ...)
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.botToken, ...)
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 2/10 in 11s
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 22s
# after restoring a valid token via config.apply:
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
# intentional stop while channel was running:
channels.stop telegram → {"channel":"telegram","accountId":"default","stopped":true}
channels.status → running=false, restartPending=false
```

- Control check: focused suite still **51 passed** on the exact post-merge head; live Telegram reconnect after token restore shows the restart chain is not permanently dead after provider close
- Observed result after fix: after a real Telegram provider close, the manager schedules restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt … in …s`) and continues the chain; intentional `channels.stop` cancels supervision without leaving a healthy account permanently unavailable; restoring credentials allows `starting provider` again
- What was not tested: multi-hour Zalo/`zalouser` production outage, Docker healthcheck path, Discord websocket (Discord API connectivity failed on this host: ECONNREFUSED / READY timeout), other channel providers beyond Telegram + the shared manager harness

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).
